source_text: Novo genere disserendi et catholicum profiteris et Manichaeo patrocinaris, dicendo nuptias et magnum bonum et magnum malum
pass_a_gloss: By a new kind of discussing you both profess yourself catholic and take the Manichaean's side, by saying that marriages are both a great good and a great evil.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: By a new kind of argument, you profess to be Catholic while taking the Manichaean’s side, saying that marriage is both a great good and a great evil.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Julian claims the catholic faith against Augustine; keep lowercase-c catholic as the universal church, not a later confessional brand.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, De nuptiis et concupiscentia 2 / On Marriage and Concupiscence); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
kind: Julian excerpt in the intermediary document
